full_judgment:
12. From the FIR lodged by PW 1 Abdul Mannan the High Court Division found, to begin with, that the motive for commission of the crime, namely, the bearing of grudge by the accused party against the informant party for not being able to purchase the Bichra has not been proved by examining the erstwhile owner of that land, noticing in the same breath that the said owner Abdul Khaleque was dead. Abdul Khaleque's sons were also not examined by the prosecution, the High Court Division observed. PW 1 also could not say whether they were paying rent for the purchased land or whether their names have been mutated in the record of rights or not. The High Court Division found that it was not at all clear what prompted the accused persons to commit murder of 4/5 persons. Then 'there is a positive finding that the motive has not been proved and "is rejected": That is how the judgment began in a case of murder of 4 persons proved by 10 eye-witnesses. 

 14. The High Court Division then found that the prosecution has deliberately suppressed some material facts. It is on record, without referring to any evidence, that while Hamid, Alfaz and Siraj chased Somedupto the Bichra, the informant party resisted them. Therefore, it held, the occurrence is an offshoot of a trivial incident that took place at the District Board Road where Somed was beaten by Hamid, Alfaz and Siraj with lathi. It was the view of the High Court Division that the prosecution has not brought on record the material facts that culminated in the onslaught. Therefore it cannot but be said that there was a free fight between the parties. May be the accused party was disproportionately stronger than the informant party, but nevertheless the whole incident occurred on the spur of the moment without there being anything to sustain any motive as suggested by the prosecution. 

 17. Narrating the prosecution case all over again but without discussing any evidence on record the High Court Division then found that nothing could be elicited by way of cross-examination of all the PWs. which can be said to be "exculpatory circumstances" sufficient to cast a reasonable doubt about the statements of prosecution witnesses. Referring to the defence argument that the witnesses are partisan and interested the High Court Division then makes a U-turn and observes, "but whether a witness is a partisan and interested or not an whatever be his attribute, in the final analysis of the evidence, the best test of his statement is its inherent worth in point of consistency, straightforwardness as tested against the physical possibilities and circumstances surrounding the events to which such testimony relate." The High Court Division relies upon the corroborating evidence of PW 18, the first investigating officer, accepts PW 12 Abdul Haque Bhuiyan as a disinterested and natural witness and gives a finding that they strongly corroborated the testimonies of PWs 1-11 and as such "there is nothing to disbelieve their statements." The High Court Division then found accused-respondent Nos. 1-6 guilty under section 304 Part-I of the Penal Code, "but the immediate cause that triggered off such serious violence being shrouded in mystery, a lesser sentence of 10 years RI with a fine may meet the ends of justice." 

 18. Leave was granted to consider the submissions of the State that there being sufficient direct evidence on record from eye witnesses, which has been accepted by the High Court Division notwithstanding some contrary findings, to the effect that respondent Nos. 1-6 had used guns and killed four persons, the High Court Division without any rhyme or reason wrongly altered their conviction from under sections 302, 149 to section 304 Part-I of the Penal Code and passed a totally inadequate sentence causing a grave miscarriage of justice. The High Court Division upon a misconception of law and facts wrongly held that the charge under section 149 is not maintainable and common object of the unlawful assembly has not been established. Leave was also granted to consider that consideration and findings as to "common object", "motive", Exception 4 to section 300 of the Penal Code have been erroneous and made in disregard of the proved facts of the case. Lastly, leave was granted to consider that the apparent inconsistencies in the findings of fact in the impugned judgment show that there has been absence of balance in the whole judgment which needs re-consideration. Leave was granted as against respondent Nos. 1-6 only and leave in respect of other accused-respondents was refused. 

 19. From what has been summarized above we have no hesitation to find that the impugned judgment is a totally unacceptable, unsatisfactory, disjointed, inherently incoherent, contradictory and confused judgment both in law and facts manifesting an alarming mindfulness of the basic principles of criminal jurisprudence and what is worse there is a total absence of any systematic consideration of evidence following the ordinary norms. It is a haphazard exercise, jumping from one topic to another, full of contradictory finding and total non-consideration of the evidence on record. 

 26. Further, the finding of the learned Judges is that the account of events which followed one after another, as given by PWs 1-2, is absurd and improbable. If we may say so, this conclusion itself without referring to any evidence on record is absurd and improbable. The prosecution did not set up an absurd and improbable case. Their case is backed up by the evidence of natural and competent eye-witnesses some of whom themselves sustained injuries at the hands of some accused persons whose conviction has been upheld under sections 326 and 324 of the Penal Code. The High Court Division found, again without evidence, that the informant party resisted the accused party and, as such, the true story has been suppressed not only by the prosecution but also by the defence. Where is the evidence that the informant party resisted the accused party when Somed was being chased? These are all surmises and it is disappointing that a Death Reference case has been dealt with by the High Court Division with the aid of surmises, conjectures and bizarre speculations rather than with the aid of evidence on record. 

 30. We would have accepted the Death Reference and restored the trial Court's sentence of death, had it not been for the fact that the respondents were sentenced to death in 1990 and were saved from the gallows by a judgment of the High Court Division, also of 1990, and that for long 8 years they had been living with the expectation that their lives had been saved, but we cannot agree with the apparently perverse decision of the High Court Division that their conviction was liable to be altered from sections 302, 149 to section 304 Part-I of the Penal Code which has absolutely no application in view of the evidence on record. We set aside the order of the High Court Division altering the conviction and sentence in the manner aforesaid and restore the conviction of the accused-respondent Nos. 1-6 as under sections 302, 149 of the Penal Code but in so far as the sentence is concerned we do not propose to impose the death sentence because of the reasons given earlier and propose instead to sentence them to imprisonment for life each, as we find that the reduction of sentence has resulted in a grave miscarriage of justice. A gruesome murder of 4 persons by gunshots has been treated in a cavalier manner. 

 31. The appeal is allowed. The conviction and sentence of accused-respondent Nos. 1-6 as modified by the High Court Division are set aside and their conviction under sections 302,149 of the Penal Code as recorded by the trial Court is affirmed. The sentence of death passed by the trial Court is, however, altered to imprisonment for life each. 

 35. After framing of the charge, the trial of a session’s case starts wherein the evidence is recorded. In a criminal trial the consideration of the evidence is of prime importance. The truth or falsity of a prosecution case is determined either in trial or in appeal on the basis of evidence on record. But unfortunately the judgment of the Division Bench of the High Court Division was totally devoid of any consideration of the evidence on record. Thus the judgment is not a legal judgment based on scrutiny of the evidence on record. 

 38. In the present case, charge was framed against the accused-respondents under sections 302,149 of the Penal Code which indicates that the accused persons by forming an unlawful assembly with a common object of committing murder committed the offence of murder of those four persons named in the charge. It is the duty of the prosecution to prove the charge under sections 302, 149 of the Penal Code by adducing evidence. It is the quality of evidence which will prove the common object of that assembly to commit the offence of murder as indicated in the charge. The learned Judges of the High Court Division made a confusion between motive and common object. Motive has nothing to do with the common object. The prosecution in a case may bring motive as an element which may be the cause of commission of an offence. But charge is the statement of facts which go to show the time, place and the manner of commission of an offence. Distinction between motive and framing of the charge ought to have been kept separate by the learned Judges of the High Court Division. But unfortunately, motive for commission of the offence and the manner and acts of commission of the offence have been confused by the learned Judges of the High Court Division. As motive for those four murders prosecution has imputed motive to the effect that the accused-respondents being unsuccessful to purchase the Bichra (attached land to homestead) of Khaleque became furious and to take revenge attacked PW 11 Somad and his relations. In the evidence of PW 1 informant Abdul Manna it is found that they purchased the Bichra and homestead of Khaleque and they are in possession of the same. It is true that the prosecution did not produce any document to show that they purchased the land and possessed it but as motive the prosecution has said that this may be the motive for the accused persons to commit the offence of murder. It is a settled principle of law that the prosecution is not bound to give any motive, more particularly in a case where the accused persons are sought to be connected with the offence by direct evidence as indicated in this case. In the case of State vs Lalu Miah reported in 39 DLR (AD) 11 7, it has been clearly stated that the prosecution is not bound to prove the motive for committing a criminal offence. An accused may be prompted by various considerations for committing an offence and it is .not always possible for the prosecution to enter into the criminal mind to pin point the motive for any offence. In the present case, the prosecution mentioned a motive and even if it is accepted that the prosecution failed to prove that motive the direct evidence of the eye-witnesses cannot be discarded. The trial Court believed the eye witnesses. The High Court Division could have as well disbelieved the same witnesses by providing valid reasons but without giving any consideration of the evidence only on the failure to prove motive a prosecution case cannot be discarded as has been done by the learned Judges of the High Court Division. As a matter of act on a total confusion the learned Judges without referring to the evidence on record at all most whimsically and illegally altered the charge from section 302,149 of the Penal Code to sections 304 Part I of the Penal Code. 

 39. On a reference to the charge we do not find that the charge is defective in any manner. The charge clearly speaks of commission of the offence of murder in pursuance of the common object of the unlawful assembly. The material question which remains to be determined by the trial Court or by the lower appellate Court is, whether the prosecution has been able to prove the charge. The prosecution is to prove that the acts of murder were done in pursuance of the common object of that unlawful assembly or such offences as the members of the unlawful assembly knew to be likely to be committed in prosecution of that object. From the consistent evidence we find that the accused persons who were members of the unlawful assembly were armed with guns, daos, ballam, balanga etc. encircled the Bichra (adjacent homestead) and fired several gun shots which injured four deceased persons. All the members of the unlawful assembly had knowledge that in prosecution of the common object of that unlawful assembly guns and other deadly weapons were to be used which might cause death. The accused persons were aggressors as they attacked the informant party without any provocation. From the weapons used and nature of injuries received by the deceased persons at the vital parts of the bodies it is palpably clear that it is a clear case of murder as defined under section 300 of the Penal Code. Apart from this, the eye-witnesses testified that accused respondent’s No. 1 and 4 inflicted gunshot injuries on deceased Chandu. Accused respondent Nos. 3 and 5 fired gun shots to deceased Suruj and accused respondent No.2 Abdul Awal assaulted deceased Azimuddin with gunshot. Accused respondent No.6 Abdur Rahman assaulted deceased Ahamed by his gun. It appears that these six accused respondents who were charged under section 302, 149 of the Penal Code also committed specific overt acts by firing from their guns. Thus it appears from the evidence on record that these accused-respondents participated in specific overt acts and, as such, there is no difficulty in finding that the accused persons were guilty of the offence constructively under section 149 of the Penal Code. It is indeed surprising that the learned Judges did not at all correctly address themselves to the question with regard to the common object of the unlawful assembly. 

 40. Further, we find that PWs 1-4 and 6-11 are the eye-witnesses. According to these witnesses, they were present in the place of occurrence and saw the entire events. Even some of the eyewitnesses got mjunes in the occurrence. PWs 2 Wahab and PW 11 Somed got injuries in the nature of incised wounds and punctured wounds on their persons. PW 16 Dr. Shafiuddin Sikder, a medical officer attached to Mitamoyee Health Center also examined these witnesses and found one incised wound and two swellings on different parts of the bodies of PWs 2 and 11 respectively. All the eyewitnesses have also stated that PWs 2 and 11 received the injuries at the time of occurrence. So the presence of these two witnesses as eyewitnesses cannot be disbelieved. PW 3 Alauddin, PW 4 Samaraj, PW 10 Malek also received injuries in the occurrence. So their presence as eye witnesses of the occurrence cannot be also be disbelieved. Apart from these witnesses who got injuries, the consistent evidence of other eyewitnesses proved that the occurrence took place in the Bichra of PW 1 where four persons of the informant party were killed by gun shots. The trial Court on an elaborate discussion of the evidence of these ten eye-witnesses believed the prosecution case. The evidence of these eye-witnesses so far as the injuries are concerned is also corroborated by the medical officer who held post-mortem examination on the four dead bodies of the deceased persons. It is indeed unfortunate that the learned Judges of the High Court Division did not consider the ocular and corroborative evidence on record and to non-consideration of the evidence has caused a great miscarriage of justice.
